analyst.summary: JSW Steel has had a genuinely good twelve months: the multi-year Bhushan Power & Steel legal fight is finally over (Supreme Court upheld its resolution plan in March 2026), the Bhushan Power business has been folded into a 50:50 joint venture with Japan's JFE Steel that brought in fresh cash, and net debt has fallen sharply, taking net-debt-to-EBITDA down from over 3x to about 1.5x in a year. Steel volumes are growing and a safeguard duty is currently protecting Indian mills from cheap Chinese and Vietnamese imports, pushing profitability per tonne up sharply. The catch is that the stock, near its 52-week high, already prices in a lot of this improvement, plus continued strong (duty-assisted) margins and years of flawless execution on an ambitious capacity-expansion plan -- while the company's actual returns on capital remain modest for a business valued this richly. On balance, this looks like a case where the good news is already reflected in the price of a still-cyclical, capital-intensive business, more than a name to hold for further re-rating.
